topline.text: NEU's national executive meets today to decide whether to press ahead with the 3 October strike ballot, after ministers offered around £500m in pension-savings funding towards the 2026-27 teacher pay award.
topline.action: Worth watching for the outcome later today — it signals whether autumn disruption is likely.

topline.text: A genuinely quiet 24-48 hours otherwise: nothing else new broke overnight across DfE, SEND, Ofsted, safeguarding or funding beyond what's already on your radar.

diary.text: NEU's national executive meets to decide its formal response to the government's pay/funding offer, including whether the 3 October ballot still proceeds.
NEU's formal strike ballot opens (if not called off), covering 280,000+ teachers; closes 15 Dec.

items.lede: NEU executive meets today to decide on the strike ballot after a £500m pension-savings offer.
items.body: Education secretary Lucy Powell told NEU general secretary Daniel Kebede that schools can use savings from reduced employer pension contributions — around £500m nationally — to help fund the 2026-27 pay award, addressing the union's objection that it wasn't fully funded. The executive meets today to decide whether the 3 October ballot still goes ahead. Figure as widely reported; today's outcome wasn't confirmed at time of writing.
items.action: Worth confirming with your finance lead once the executive's decision lands — it affects whether disruption is likely this term.

box.text: Extra funding ministers say schools can draw from pension-contribution savings to help fund the 2026-27 teacher pay award, addressing NEU's 'fully funded' objection.
